title: How El Niño Changes Weather Worldwide
description: How weakening Pacific winds reshape rain, the jet stream and marine life, from NOAA and NASA.
narration: How can warm water in one ocean change weather worldwide? El Niño is a Pacific Ocean condition so big that it affects weather around the world. Normally, strong equatorial winds push warm surface water west toward Indonesia. In some years those winds weaken, and the warm water piles up along South America. The warmer water pushes the Pacific jet stream south of its usual position. Clouds over the warm water dump much more rain than usual on the Americas, while other regions can face drought. Off the Pacific coast, upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water weakens or stops.

claims.sentence: El Niño is a Pacific Ocean condition so big that it affects weather around the world.
claims.quote: El Niño is a condition that sometimes occurs in the Pacific Ocean, but it is so big that it affects weather all over the world.

claims.sentence: Normally, strong equatorial winds push warm surface water west toward Indonesia.
claims.quote: Normally, strong winds along the equator push the warm surface water near South America westward toward Indonesia.

claims.sentence: In some years those winds weaken, and the warm water piles up along South America.
claims.quote: However, in the fall and winter of some years, these winds are much weaker than usual. They actually blow the other way (toward South America instead of Indonesia) in October. So the warm surface water along the equator piles up along the coast of South America

claims.sentence: The warmer water pushes the Pacific jet stream south of its usual position.
claims.quote: The warmer waters cause the Pacific jet stream to move south of its neutral position.

claims.sentence: Clouds over the warm water dump much more rain than usual on the Americas, while other regions can face drought.
claims.quote: These clouds move inland and dump much more rain than usual in South and Central America and in the United States. Meanwhile, other parts of the world can suffer drought.

claims.sentence: Off the Pacific coast, upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water weakens or stops.
claims.quote: During normal conditions, upwelling brings water from the depths to the surface; this water is cold and nutrient rich. During El Niño, upwelling weakens or stops altogether.
